clue.text: Military briefing given in tutorial

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier in the military
a briefing is instruction given, so a lesson

explanation.surface: A tutorial consists of an army briefing on tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Military' reads as an adjective on 'briefing', but it gives the soldier's rank on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-to-one tutorial with a teacher is individual tuition given away from a class.

clue.text: Joints for midshipmen

explanation.surface: Cannabis cigarettes handed round among junior naval officers.
explanation.walkthrough: In old naval slang midshipmen were called reefers because they went aloft to reef the sails.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: cannabis cigarettes are rolled smokes, and naval slang named junior officers after reefing sails.

clue.text: Permit bend to be put in Roman road

indicators.note: to be put in tells us the bend goes inside the road

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia
an S-bend is a bend shaped like that letter

explanation.surface: Planning permission is given to straighten a bend on an old Roman road.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document stamped in a passport grants entry, so it is an official permit.

clue.text: Young swimmer returns digital audio tape by post

indicators.note: returns asks for the abbreviation to be turned round and read the other way

parts.note: DAT is the standard abbreviation for digital audio tape
a pole is an upright post

explanation.surface: A young swimmer sends back a recording on tape through the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns DAT into TAD; 'by' simply joins it to POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs begin life as aquatic larvae that swim with tails before growing legs.

clue.text: Keep going at work later than everyone else

definitions.text: at work later than everyone else

explanation.surface: Someone keeps grinding on, staying in the office after all colleagues have gone home.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure to the end is one sense; the other is literally being the final person to leave.

clue.text: What the spirits drinker likes to hit

explanation.surface: A whisky drinker who enjoys a punch-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig of neat liquor is one sense; to punch someone hard is the other.

clue.text: Could it play an eight-part autumnal work?

parts.note: October is an autumn month, abbreviated OCT
opus is Latin for a musical work

explanation.surface: A question whether some musician could perform an autumn composition in eight parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a creature with eight arms might manage eight parts at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-armed sea creature could, jokingly, handle eight instrumental lines simultaneously.

clue.text: Confessed to knocking over the coffee jar

explanation.surface: Someone owned up to upsetting the coffee jar on the kitchen floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means revealed a secret, and literally it describes coffee beans spilled from a tipped jar.

clue.text: Mean to say that a little lass is light-fingered?

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name, here a small girl
a light-fingered person is stealing, so pinching

explanation.surface: Asking whether a small girl is a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to say that' introduces the pun: read as name plus verb, it describes a girl stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy people save every coin, so the hyphenated adjective means miserly.

clue.text: Gratified to find petition getting some French backing

parts.note: a plea is a formal request or petition

indicators.note: backing means the French word is read in reverse

parts.note: des is French for some

explanation.surface: Someone is gratified that a petition has gained support from some French people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns DES into SED; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratified and happy are synonyms describing satisfaction.

clue.text: Try to sink a ship that carries coal

explanation.surface: A plan to sink a collier.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a vessel deliberately is one sense; the other is the bucket used to hold coal by a fireplace.

clue.text: Stagger back to look at the girls

indicators.note: back says the synonym is read backwards

parts.note: to reel is to stagger

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers back to ogle the women.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle lecherously at women with a sly sideways look.

clue.text: The driving force of Doctor Hill

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, an army doctor
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Asking what motivates a doctor named Hill.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a rocky hilltop in English moorland, especially Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine supplies the power that drives a machine.

clue.text: Appeal to shut up? Quite the opposite!

definitions.text: Appeal to shut up? Quite the opposite!

parts.words: Appeal to shut up? Quite the opposite!
parts.note: the request is not to close but its contrary, the plea one makes at a locked door or a closed mouth

explanation.surface: A plea for silence, then a twist saying it is the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse of closing is unfastening, so a request to unclose is the word meant.

clue.text: Avoid telling who wrote Jerusalem'

explanation.surface: Dodging the question of who wrote a famous hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: Hubert Parry set Blake's poem 'Jerusalem' to music; it is a patriotic English hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect a question or blow is one sense; the composer Hubert of that surname is the other.

clue.text: Overall way to gather the threads together

definitions.text: way to gather the threads together

explanation.surface: Overall, a method for drawing loose ends together.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose work garment worn over clothes is one sense; decorative stitching that gathers fabric into tight pleats is the other.

clue.text: Nation which Lawrence created by will-power?

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, by his initials
a state is a nation

explanation.surface: A country founded by Lawrence of Arabia through sheer determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will-power' is a pun: a person dying with a legal will has property passed by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having left a valid legal will at death, so an estate distributed by that document.

clue.text: Stop writing now that paper costs more

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper
prices that are up cost more

explanation.surface: An invigilator calls for pens down; the newspaper has gone up in price.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase an examiner calls at the end of an exam when the allotted period has ended.

clue.text: Pointed comment from English pork and lamb suppliers

parts.note: a pig supplies pork
a ram sires lambs, so supplies them

explanation.surface: A sharp remark from English farmers who raise pigs and sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A short witty saying with a sting is a barbed remark.

clue.text: A number, for instance, having to go in between

indicators.note: having to go in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: inter is the Latin prefix for between
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: Someone must step in to mediate, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number without fractions is a kind of numeral.

clue.text: Caustic extract from Grimm or Dante

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A biting passage quoted from the Brothers Grimm or Dante.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting or sarcastic wit is described as acid, corrosive, cutting.

clue.text: Sailor boy who made it to the White House

definitions.text: who made it to the White House

parts.note: jack, as in Jack Tar, is a sailor
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A sailor's son who rose to become President.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Jackson was the seventh US President.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew of that surname reached the presidency, the seventh to occupy the American executive mansion.

clue.text: Legal administration is on the rocks

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Legal administration is on the rocks (7)': ICE comes from 'on the rocks' but no word gives JUST; 'is' looks like a misread of 'just' or a word is missing, and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Legal administration is on the rocks

clue.text: Glib speech about an old gunman's best friend

indicators.note: about means the patter goes around the next word

parts.note: a spiel is a glib sales patter

explanation.surface: A smooth-talker speaks of an elderly hunter's dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A gundog breed used by shooters to flush and retrieve game.

clue.text: Some dine at six on them

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people have dinner at six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads with the rest: diners dine on food, so 'on them' means the grub.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for food, what diners dine upon.

clue.text: Bull-headed, reckless and self-assertive

indicators.note: headed says take just the head, or opening letter, of the word Bull

parts.note: rash means reckless

explanation.surface: A description of a stubborn, impetuous, pushy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull-headed' looks like stubborn, but it gives only the first letter of 'Bull'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash people are bold and pushy, confidently forward.

clue.text: Composer the Welsh name with affection

explanation.surface: A musician whom the people of Wales call by a pet name.
explanation.walkthrough: In Welsh this word is a term of endearment, like 'dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian, the German baroque musician, is one sense; the Welsh endearment meaning dear is the other.

clue.text: Time to reflect on a specific location

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the following letter
to reflect means the time word is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Time to think about a particular place.
explanation.definitionFit: A region or zone is a particular place.

clue.text: Penny on petrol causes sharp intake of breath

indicators.note: on here means the penny is added onto the petrol word

parts.note: gas is the American word for petrol

explanation.surface: A penny rise in fuel price makes drivers gasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick sudden breath drawn in from shock.

clue.text: Grain that is cultivated in Africa

indicators.note: cultivated, like worked soil, says these letters are turned over and rearranged

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Grain grown in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African country, so a place within that continent.

clue.text: I smuggled Scotsman from Middle-Eastern country

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so ran
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to smuggling a Scot out of a Middle Eastern state.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Persia's modern state, an adjective of nationality.

clue.text: Compose anagrams, but become disenchanted

explanation.surface: A crossword setter rearranges words and loses the magic.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is cryptic: making anagrams breaks up how words are spelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrambling letters disrupts spelling; the idiom means ending an enchantment or illusion.
